title: On the "Mind's Eye"
synopsis: The Chinese word "心眼“, which literally means the "mind's eye", can be used to convey a wide range of personality traits. Are there people in your social circle who match these descriptions?

fullText.simplified:
说“心眼”

    你听过“缺心眼”或者“没心眼”吗？在中文里，“心眼”是一个非常有趣的词。它常常用来形容一个人的性格、聪明程度，或者他对别人的态度。
    “缺心眼”和“没心眼”这两个词看起来很像，但其实意思不完全一样。
    “缺心眼”是说一个人有点儿傻，不太懂人情世故，也不太会动脑子。有时候别人已经在暗示什么了，他还一头雾水。比如说：“他真是有点缺心眼，老板话里话外都提醒了，他还没听出来。”虽然“缺心眼”听起来像是在批评，但朋友之间有时也会用它来开玩笑。
    而“没心眼”呢，更多的是说一个人很单纯，没有坏心思，不会耍小聪明。这个词通常是用来夸人的，说这个人很老实、值得信任。只是有时候，如果太“没心眼”，也可能意味着太老实，不太会保护自己。比如说：“她人特别好，没什么心眼，跟谁都能相处得来。”
    简单来说，“缺心眼”是“傻得让人着急”，而“没心眼”则是“傻得让人喜欢”。一个是“脑子不够用”，一个是“心地特别好”。在日常生活中，如果你想夸一个人单纯善良，那就可以说他“没心眼”；但如果你觉得某人太迟钝、太不会看人眼色，那可能就会说他“缺心眼”了。
    除了这两个词，“心眼”还有很多其他有趣的说法。
    比如，“心眼多”。这个词有好有坏。好的一面是，这个人聪明，脑子转得快，做事有办法；不好的一面是，他太会算计了，让人觉得不容易信任。我们可以这么用：“她心眼多，做事很有办法，老板很喜欢她。”或者“他这人心眼太多，跟他说话得特别小心。”
    再比如，“小心眼”是说一个人太爱计较，不够大方，容易生气、记仇。比如，我们可以这样说：“他这个人有点儿小心眼，你一句话说错了，他能记很久。”
    相反，“心眼好”则是一个非常正面的说法，表示这个人善良、乐于助人。我们可以这么用：“奶奶虽然不识字，但是心眼特别好，邻居们都喜欢她。”
    还有一个常见的说法是“长个心眼”，它常常用来提醒别人要多留心，不要太轻信别人。比如：“每次被他骗了你还帮他，你能不能长个心眼啊？”
    虽然“心眼”只是一个词，但搭配不同的词语，就能表达出很多种性格特点。“心眼”这个词既能夸人，也能批评人，用得好，会让你的表达更地道。
    你呢？你觉得自己是个“没心眼”的人，还是“心眼多”的人？你的朋友中有没有“心眼好”的，或者“有点小心眼”的人呢？

說“心眼”

    你聽過“缺心眼”或者“沒心眼”嗎？在中文裡，“心眼”是一個非常有趣的詞。它常常用來形容一個人的性格、聰明程度，或者他對別人的態度。
    “缺心眼”和“沒心眼”這兩個詞看起來很像，但其實意思不完全一樣。
    “缺心眼”是說一個人有點兒傻，不太懂人情世故，也不太會動腦子。有時候別人已經在暗示什麼了，他還一頭霧水。比如說：“他真是有點缺心眼，老闆話裡話外都提醒了，他還沒聽出來。”雖然“缺心眼”聽起來像是在批評，但朋友之間有時也會用它來開玩笑。
    而“沒心眼”呢，更多的是說一個人很單純，沒有壞心思，不會耍小聰明。這個詞通常是用來誇人的，說這個人很老實、值得信任。只是有時候，如果太“沒心眼”，也可能意味著太老實，不太會保護自己。比如說：“她人特別好，沒什麼心眼，跟誰都能相處得來。”
    簡單來說，“缺心眼”是“傻得讓人著急”，而“沒心眼”則是“傻得讓人喜歡”。一個是“腦子不夠用”，一個是“心地特別好”。在日常生活中，如果你想誇一個人單純善良，那就可以說他“沒心眼”；但如果你覺得某人太遲鈍、太不會看人眼色，那可能就會說他“缺心眼”了。
    除了這兩個詞，“心眼”還有很多其他有趣的說法。
    比如，“心眼多”。這個詞有好有壞。好的一面是，這個人聰明，腦子轉得快，做事有辦法；不好的一面是，他太會算計了，讓人覺得不容易信任。我們可以這麼用：“她心眼多，做事很有辦法，老闆很喜歡她。”或者“他這人心眼太多，跟他說話得特別小心。”
    再比如，“小心眼”是說一個人太愛計較，不夠大方，容易生氣、記仇。比如，我們可以這樣說：“他這個人有點兒小心眼，你一句話說錯了，他能記很久。”
    相反，“心眼好”則是一個非常正面的說法，表示這個人善良、樂於助人。我們可以這麼用：“奶奶雖然不識字，但是心眼特別好，鄰居們都喜歡她。”
    還有一個常見的說法是“長個心眼”，它常常用來提醒別人要多留心，不要太輕信別人。比如：“每次被他騙了你還幫他，你能不能長個心眼啊？”
    雖然“心眼”只是一個詞，但搭配不同的詞語，就能表達出很多種性格特點。“心眼”這個詞既能誇人，也能批評人，用得好，會讓你的表達更地道。
    你呢？你覺得自己是個“沒心眼”的人，還是“心眼多”的人？你的朋友中有沒有“心眼好”的，或者“有點小心眼”的人呢？

sentences.simplified: 用得好，会让你的表达更地道。
sentences.traditional: 用得好，會讓你的表達更地道。
sentences.pinyin: yòng de hǎo huì ràng nǐ de biǎo dá gèng dì dao
sentences.english: The word “心眼” can be used both to compliment and to criticize people.
If used well, it can make what you’re conveying sound more authentic.

sentences.simplified: 你呢？你觉得自己是个“没心眼”的人，还是“心眼多”的人？
sentences.traditional: 你呢？你覺得自己是個“沒心眼”的人，還是“心眼多”的人？
sentences.pinyin: nǐ ne nǐ jué de zì jǐ shì ge méi xīn yǎn de rén hái shi xīn yǎn duō de rén

sentences.simplified: 你的朋友中有没有“心眼好”的，或者“有点小心眼”的人呢？
sentences.traditional: 你的朋友中有沒有“心眼好”的，或者“有點小心眼”的人呢？
sentences.pinyin: nǐ de péng you zhōng yǒu méi yǒu xīn yǎn hǎo de huò zhě yǒu diǎn xiǎo xīn yǎn de rén ne
sentences.english: How about you? Do you think of yourself as a “没心眼” person or a “心眼多” person?

sentence_translations: On the “Mind’s Eye”
Have you heard of “缺心眼” or “没心眼”? In Chinese, “心眼” [mind’s eye] is a very interesting word.
It is often used to describe a person’s character, level of intelligence, or their attitude toward others.
The phrases “缺心眼” and “没心眼” look very similar, but their meanings are actually not exactly the same.
“缺心眼” means a person is a bit foolish, doesn’t really understand the ways of the world, and isn’t very good at thinking things through.
Sometimes when others are already hinting at something, they are still completely clueless.
For example: “He’s really a bit slow to pick up on things.
His boss reminded him both directly and indirectly, but he still didn’t catch on.”
Although “缺心眼” sounds like a criticism, friends sometimes use it jokingly among themselves.
As for “没心眼”, it more often describes a person who is very pure, does not have bad intentions, and does not play clever tricks.
This phrase is usually used to compliment someone, saying that the person is honest and trustworthy.
However, sometimes being too “没心眼” can also mean being too honest and not very good at protecting oneself.
For example: “She is especially kind, has no hidden motives, and can get along well with everyone.”
Simply put, “缺心眼” is “foolishness that makes other people anxious”, while “没心眼” is “foolishness that makes other people fond of you”.
One is “not having enough brainpower”, and the other is “having a particularly kind heart”.
In daily life, if you want to compliment someone for being pure and kind-hearted, you can say they are “没心眼”.
But if you think someone is too slow, or not good at reading people’s expressions, you might say they are “缺心眼”.
In addition to these two phrases, there are many other interesting expressions with the word “心眼”.
For example, “心眼多”. This phrase can be both positive and negative.
On the positive side, this person is smart, quick-witted, and can get things done.
On the negative side, they are too calculating, making it difficult for people to trust them.
We can use it like this: “She is very shrewd and gets things done. The boss likes her a lot.”
Or, “He is very calculating, so you have to be particularly careful when talking to him.”
Another example, “小心眼” describes a person who is overly petty, not generous enough, and prone to getting angry and holding grudges.
For example, we can say: “He is a bit petty. If you say something wrong, he’ll remember it for a long time.”
On the contrary, “心眼好” is a very positive expression, indicating that this person is kind and willing to help others.
We can use it like this: “Although the old lady is illiterate, she is very kind-hearted, and all the neighbors like her.”
Another common expression is “长个心眼”, which is often used to remind others to be more vigilant and not to trust others too easily.
For example: “Every time he deceives you, you still help him. Can’t you grow some sense?”
Although “心眼” is just one word, when combined with different words, it can express a wide range of personality traits.
The word “心眼” can be used both to compliment and to criticize people.
If used well, it can make what you’re conveying sound more authentic.
How about you? Do you think of yourself as a “没心眼” person or a “心眼多” person?
Do you have any friends who are “心眼好” or “有点小心眼”?
